title: Remove the sigstore package to downgrade provenance enforcement to a warning

prerequisites: An attacker who already has write access to node_modules (can delete the installed sigstore package) and wants to install a package whose provenance would fail to verify
attacker.goal: Slip a package past provenance enforcement by making the verification tool absent, so the check degrades to a warning instead of blocking.

startingState: sigstore was installed; the attacker deletes it, then installs a package with a bad/absent provenance bundle. Because the tool is now missing, provenance cannot be evaluated and the bootstrap-deadlock fix degrades it to a warning.
vulnerableVersion: n/a — documented limit: the tool-absent degradation is a deliberate availability tradeoff (SafeInstall must be bootstrappable), accepted in exchange for a residual attacker path here
expectedVerdict: known-gap: provenance is NOT enforced while sigstore is absent; the install emits a loud per-package 'provenance NOT verified — sigstore not installed' warning, and the independent layers (release age, typo-squat, untrusted source, install scripts) still apply
regressionTest: tests/policy.test.ts > still blocks a genuinely invalid attestation even in the same strict config (attacker case)
provenance: The residual introduced by the provenance-tooling-bootstrap fix (issue #56). Kept as a first-class known-gap so it cannot be silently relabelled 'defended': closing it needs tool-presence enforcement (e.g. an opt-in provenance.requireTooling that pre-installs sigstore out of band) without re-breaking bootstrap. An attacker who can delete node_modules already has broad local write access — a different, larger threat model.
